reviews.review: Point, shoot, click. Nice. Honestly really great game and highly recommend it. Even if you "only" have 1 friend to play it with.
Great gameplay, great combat system. It's not perfect, but its quite close. If you haven't already, I highly recommend getting this.

Disclaimer:
I purchased a dirt-cheap key for this game, since I was well aware of how terrible it was (I am one of those guys who cancelled their pre-order back then).
I expected this game to be the worst.
And the game managed to crush my expectations in the worst way possible.
The cutscenes are just-bland gorefests that add nothing to the story. While the game makes half an attempt to give you these "the walking dead vibes", it fails to tell an even marginally coherent story. The intro-cutscene is the only cutscene that even attempts to build a backstory, after that each cutscene I watched within the first act just boils down to generic gory zombie shooting.

the card-system is 'okay', but it doesn't really change that much really (it can buff special infected, nothing that you wouldn't find on an L4D2 custom server or in L4D2 arcade), health in this game works really weird, and the bosses are just bullet sponges with a braindead AI. You'll find more creative custom bosses in L4D2, which says a LOT, considering that L4D2 didn't really intend for bosses to exist (but mappers were able to make it work regardless, while B4B dropped the modding-aspect altogether).

The game uses a Call of Duty control-scheme (which I don't like, being used to this game's so-called "predecessor"), but it still feels more stiff than actual Call-of-Duty does. Call of Duty's controls -while not m favourite- at least feel responsive, while B4B just feels like playing COD while drunk.

The zombies in B4B also fail to make the same impact as they do in COD (since the common infected are CODs strength), while the SI in B4B (which are Left4Dead's strength) just feel like bullet sponges that must rely on the crowd to make an impact (the SI are too slow to do anything on their own and the allied AI will spot and mark them through walls mere seconds after they spawned in, giving away their precise location, like a built-in X-Ray)

I got more to say, but honestly, everybody knows that this game blows, I won't waste my breath here any further.
If you pick this game up, make sure you don't pay double digits. Left4Dead2 is 2 bucks (while on sale) and it objectively contains so much more value, regardless of whether you actually like B4B or not, so paying more than a single-digit value for B4B would be an outright scam. But really, either play COD or L4D2. B4B tried to blend the two together but they half-assed both of their most vital gameplay-aspects beyond the point of salvation. Or I guess, there would be a potential for salvation, but considering that this game still plays like a beta build, I wouldn't get my hopes up about the devs actually being granted the time and resources they'd need to save this mess.

unrelated PSA: Make sure that you de-trollify your steam username when logging in for the first time. B4B will assume that your username is your proper username and auto-assign a static-ingame ID to your B4B account which you can't edit once assigned. It does display a textbox to tease you, but you can't actually click into it or edit the ID. The devs really don't know anything about the platform their core-audience uses.
[in case you are curious, I had a troll-username because we encountered a funny survivor-model glitch in L4D2 the day prior, and I temporarily changed my username to fit the visual glitch, and I forgot to change it back before launching B4B since I didn't expect the devs to be THIS dumb, and how could I, really?]

TLDR: I expected this disgrace of a game to be bad, but it's just so much worse than I could have ever hoped for (it's far worse than the review-videos I watched suggested, and they were already purely negative to begin with. This game is so bad, that words and videos can't even communicate it. I'm waiting for AVGN to pick this up). And here I thought I should give the game a fair chance - and the game blew it big time.

I kinda want to feel sorry for the devs, had their marketing department marketed this game differently, it might have sold just fine - but at the same time, the game ultimately still feels kinda unfinished. To reiterate: the AI is literally able to spot enemies through the walls and forwards their location to the player (x-ray-style). The devs weren't granted enough time to patch even the most obvious holes (which is likely Warner's fault), and I can hardly recommend this game in this state.

I'd assume that you can have some fun with it (if you pick it up for less than ten bucks and invite a crossplay-friend who doesn't have a PC to play L4D), but then again, you can also have fun by playing shovelware. This doesn't mean that you would voluntarily do this to yourself for more than a few hours though.
